note: A warm-up (DayShape2): part 2 of the guitar warm-up run, picked by its kind and never for a path step. The spider as a short warm-up at a slow tempo that moves, apart from the path's spider block: a warm-up is a block of its own because `kind` is the block's.

exercise.title: The spider, slowly
exercise.why: Four fingers on four frets in a row makes every finger press in turn, so a slow spider wakes all four before a chord or a scale needs them.

cells.text:
Press Play below to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}. The tab under it shows the spider: on each string, frets 5, 6, 7 and 8 with fingers 1, 2, 3 and 4, one note per beat.
Start on the low E string and play the four notes on every string up to the high e string, then come back down the same way.
Press each note only as hard as it needs to ring, and practice until your hand stays still and only the fingers move.
